newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Olympic javelin silver medallist Louise McPaul was added to the Australian national team headed for the world athletics championships in Athens in August. However she aggravated a chronic back injury during the selection trials and will be unable to contest any of the lead-up competitions, an important aspect of her preparations for Athens. Page 21
Australian Scott Draper claimed his best performance yet by defeating No.2 seed Michael Chang in the second round of the Stella Artois tournament at Queens club. Page 21

Australian cricket coach Geoff Marsh wants the Australian Cricket Board to include more bowlers in larger squads to avoid the high attrition rate experienced in this Ashes tour, following Andy Bichel's return to Australia with a back injury. Page 22
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian dual Olympic sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor has spent two physically hard months running 500 metres in water to strengthen her bad back in preparation for the Athens world championships in August. Page 44

Australian Socceroo veteran Robbie Slater has cautioned against complacency following the team's recent 13-0 trouncing of the Solomon Islands. While it was Australia's sixth straight win under coach Terry Venables, Slater said it was difficult to evaluate the real standard of Australia's performance given the quality of opposition. Page 43

The Australian Rugby League will not discipline New South Wales selector John Raper over an emotional outburst after Wednesday's State of Origin match. The incident occurred after NSW Blues' coach Tom Raudonikis decided against fielding Raper's son, Aaro, in the Melbourne match. Page 44
THE AGE

The Melbourne Tigers basketball team's American import Jarvis Lang could have his career cut short by a degenerative knee condition which was discovered during a recent operation. Lang, 25, was a member of the United States' gold medal-winning team at the under-20 world championships. Page D13

One of the Victorian breeding industry's most durable stallions, Cardinal, was put down on veterinary advice yesterday. While Cardinal was never sound to make an impact on the racecourse, the stud sired winners of about A$3.6 million and numerous classy et-track performers including Phoenix Rising, Vatican Lass, Friar's Delight and Cardinal's Fury. Page D12

Tennis Australia has named Australia's Davis Cup captain John Newcombe as stand-in captain of the Fed Cup team to play Spain on the Gold Coast next month in a world group qualifying tie. Newcombe will be standing in for Lesley Bowrey who will be in the Uited States for his induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Page D11
THE HERALD SUN
Two of Australia's promising young pacers, Ted Demmler's boom New Zealand import Captain Rufus and Tasmanian gelding Northern Brewer will face-off over 2380m at Moonee Valley tomorrow night. Page 97.

Australian Football League's Western Bulldogs player Brad Wira claimed Geelong player Garry Hocking broke his nose before he allegedly grabbed Hocking's testicles. Hocking received a one-match suspension on a striking charge. Page 112.

Melbourne captain Gary Lyon hopes to be back in training by Christmas if surgery to relieve his back injury in successful. Lyon will be admitted next week to repair his damaged disc and will not be playing this season. Page 108.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Dean Jones has quit as captain of Derbyshire because of the anti-Australian sentiment of his senior players. Jones' exit from English county cricket followed his stewardship of the long suffering Derbyshire to second place in the county champinships last season, the highest finish the club has finished since 1936. Page 128.

The Australian rowing team leaves tomorrow for a three-month tour of Europe, culminating with the world championships in September. The team will be defending their position as the top ranked rowing nation, having won six medals, including two gold, at lst year's Olympic Games. Page 121.

Australian soccer team will face Tahiti in the Oceania World Cup qualifying round to be played at Parramatta Stadium tonight. Coach terry Venables will field a vastly differently side to the team that trashed the Solomon Islands 13-0. Page 121.
